transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CSM), Samir (Montage ML), Dana (Montage PM), Liam (Montage Sec), plus one attendee listed as Speaker 4

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to review quality eval results from last week's prompt tuning, discuss any regressions, confirm guardrails for PHI redaction, and agree next steps for final pilot benchmark.

Topics:
- Recent regression on discharge-summary prompts
- Scoring thresholds and weighting (precision vs recall)
- Guardrails / redaction heuristics and audit logs
- Next benchmark run and deliverables

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in — can you hear me ok?
[00:08] Samir: yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Priya: great, i'll share my screen in a sec with the eval dashboard, but first quick rundown of what we ran: last week we took the production prompt set v0.9, applied the guardrail filters you requested, and then ran a 1k sample eval across the clinical note subset. we also tested two new prompt variants, v0.9a and v0.9b, plus reduced temperature settings.
[00:31] Dana: just to be clear — the regression you saw last time was on discharge summary where it started omitting follow-up steps, right?
[00:37] Priya: correct, that was the main pain. the flow here—initially v0.9 had a recall dip on the follow-up-action slot down to 72% from baseline 88%. so we tuned prompting and added a targeted example in the few-shot context.
[00:55] Liam: also important from security: anything we do can't leak PHI in completions, we still need proof of redaction effectiveness. Zach from infra wants the audit logs to show redaction hits.
[01:04] Jordan: yep noted. Priya, can you walk through the scorecards? there were a lot of numbers in the spreadsheet.
[01:10] Priya: pulling up the dashboard — ok, so columns are slot-accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and a business-weighted score we calculated: 0.6 * recall + 0.4 * precision for action-type extraction since you prioritized recall. for v0.9 baseline: slot F1 0.81, recall 0.88, precision 0.75. for v0.9a (few-shot + explicit instruction) recall rose to 0.92, precision 0.72, F1 0.8. v0.9b (prompt reorder + guardrail examples) recall 0.90, precision 0.78, F1 0.84.
[01:45] Samir: so v0.9b actually has the best F1, but v0.9a best recall — which do we pick?
[01:50] Priya: depends on tradeoffs, if you need missing follow-ups minimized pick v0.9a, but if you want overall balanced accuracy v0.9b. worth noting computationally v0.9a added a longer context length so token cost went up approx 12%.
[02:06] Dana: token cost is ok within pilot but production needs to stay under our budget targets. we prefer v0.9b if quality differences are small. also curious about hallucination rates — any improvement?
[02:15] Priya: hallucination as measured by extraneous-action tokens dropped slightly for both variants; v0.9b had the lowest hallucination rate 4.1% vs baseline 6.7%. the regression we saw earlier was an edge-case where the model rewrote the follow-up into an ambiguous sentence, so extraction failed. we added a guardrail that forces canonical bullet format when we detect follow-up content.
[02:38] [02:40] Speaker 4: i think for regulatory review we also need the redaction false negatives numbers — like how many PHI tokens got through.
[02:47] Liam: yes please, that's a blocker for our security sign-off.
[02:50] Priya: on redaction — we ran the redaction filter pre and post generation; redaction false negatives were 0.3% in the eval (sanitized dataset) but full production could be higher until we test on real traffic. we also log redaction hits to audit event stream, that's in the security brief.
[03:06] Jordan: Samir, do you feel comfortable moving forward with v0.9b for the next benchmark run?
[03:11] Samir: i think yes, but two asks: 1) can you re-run v0.9b with temp 0.0 and 0.3 so we see determinism tradeoffs, and 2) can we get confusion matrices by symptom type?
[03:21] Priya: yes to both, we already have the harness to sweep temps — should be quick. confusion matrices by symptom type we'll need your annotation mapping, Samir.
[03:28] Samir: i'll attach mapping after call.
[03:31] Dana: quick question about regression detection — how are we surfacing regressions automatically? last week we only found it via manual review.
[03:38] Priya: good point; we configured a regression alert in the eval harness that flags >5% drop in weighted score for a prompt set. we also export per-prompt diffs so you can triage which prompt caused the drop. we can add more granular alerts per-slot.
[03:52] Samir: can alerts go to our slack channel?
[03:54] Alex: yes we can configure webhook -> slack, and include a link to the artifact in S3. we'll send the instructions in a follow-up.
[04:01] Liam: on the compliance front — Jordan you mentioned SOC2 docs. can we get details on encryption at rest and KMS key control?
[04:08] Jordan: absolutely, i'll send the SOC2 workbook and the KMS architecture note. quick summary: customer data in Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to use customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS; for hosted we use envelope encryption and can provide audit logs.
[04:20] Liam: and for VPC peering vs private deployment — is KV cache stored in your infra? any chance of meatadata leakage? (sic metadata)
[04:28] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral in the serving runtime and can be configured per-tenant to not persist to disk; in Dedicated we can pin cache to customer nodes. there is a small chance of metadata in logs we scrub — we have a guideline for log redaction.
[04:41] Samir: okay that matches what we need; can you include the log retention window options?
[04:45] Jordan: yes, we'll include retention options and how to configure log scrubbing.
[04:49] [05:00] Priya: back to quality — i want to highlight one odd regression: in the oncology symptom class some examples mis-labeled 'aspirin' as an intervention not an OTC med, caused by tokenization boundary in the prompt. we added a tokenization-aware example which fixed most cases. minor labeling noise still persists at ~2%.
[05:15] Dana: is that from the model or our annotation guidelines?
[05:18] Priya: mostly model, but guidelines can help; we'll mark those examples for re-annotation.
[05:22] Samir: regarding scoring, can we get per-customer-weighted score? the business cares more about missed follow-ups than minor label noise.
[05:29] Priya: yes we used a weighted score already; we'll export an interactive CSV where you can set weights and re-evaluate.
[05:36] Jordan: some housekeeping — we'll share the updated prompt set (v0.9b) and the eval CSV; priya will re-run temp sweeps; samir to send mapping and edge-case prompts; liam wants the redaction FN numbers and SOC2 workbook.
[05:50] Samir: timeline — can we get the re-run results by Friday?
[05:53] Priya: yes, we'll aim for Mar 6 EOD.
[05:56] Jordan: perfect. any blockers we missed?
[06:00] Liam: just to reiterate, security needs the audit log schema and redaction proofs.
[06:04] Jordan: we'll include those.
[06:06] Dana: also, please include a short note on cost delta for v0.9b vs baseline in the CSV so we can include in the procurement packet.
[06:12] Jordan: noted.
[06:14] Alex: i'll follow up on Slack with the webhook setup and upload locations.
[06:18] Priya: ok that's it from me. thanks everyone.
[06:21] Jordan: thanks all — recap: Redwood to share v0.9b artifacts, run temp sweep, share CSV and SOC2/KMS docs; Montage to send annotations and edge prompts. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time unless urgent.
